finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. An attacker can make the server request arbitrary URLs, including internal services, localhost, and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body returned via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: Route /fetch registered to the fetch handler
target is read from the request query string
target is passed directly to http.Get
Upstream response body is written back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, or IP validation. The `allowed` allowlist at main.go:9 is not consulted in this handler. No SSRF-safe dialer or custom http.Client is used. Redirects are followed by default.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 pass the unauthenticated query param `target` straight to http.Get with no validation, and main.go:22 copies the response back; the allowlist at main.go:9 is only used in the separate /safe handler (main.go:27), and /fetch is registered at main.go:41.
